citations.title: Momentum crashes
citations.author: Daniel, Kent and Moskowitz, Tobias J.
citations.claim: This paper examines momentum strategies in equity ETFs and finds that momentum exhibits significant crash risk during market rebounds following severe declines, particularly in 2009 and beyond. The authors propose a dynamic momentum strategy that adjusts exposure based on market conditions to mitigate crash risk while maintaining returns.

citations.title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
citations.author: Asness, Clifford S. et al.
citations.claim: This study explores value and momentum strategies across multiple asset classes, including ETFs representing equity sectors. The authors demonstrate that combining value and momentum in ETF portfolios yields significant risk-adjusted returns, with backtests from 2010 showing consistent outperformance over buy-and-hold strategies.

citations.title: Volatility Targeting: Why and How
citations.author: Fleming, Jeff and Kirby, Chris
citations.claim: The authors investigate volatility-targeting strategies in ETFs, showing that scaling exposure inversely to realized volatility improves risk-adjusted returns. Backtests from 2010 onwards on broad market and sector ETFs indicate reduced drawdowns and enhanced Sharpe ratios compared to static allocations.

citations.title: Mean Reversion in Stock Index Futures and ETFs
citations.author: Dunham, Lee M. and Friesen, Geoffrey C.
citations.claim: This paper analyzes mean reversion strategies in stock index ETFs, finding exploitable short-term inefficiencies post-2010. The authors show that mean-reverting trades based on deviation from moving averages generate statistically significant returns, particularly in high-liquidity ETFs.

citations.title: Regime-Switching Models for ETF Strategies
citations.author: Kritzman, Mark et al.
citations.claim: This research applies regime-switching models to ETF trading, identifying distinct market states (e.g., high vs. low volatility) and tailoring strategies accordingly. Backtests from 2010-2015 on sector ETFs like XLK and XLF show improved returns when allocations shift based on detected regimes.

citations.title: Carry
citations.author: Koijen, Ralph S.J. et al.
citations.claim: This paper explores carry strategies across asset classes, including ETFs tied to equity sectors. The authors find that carry, defined as expected return from holding an asset, can be harvested in ETFs with high dividend yields or roll yields, with backtests post-2010 showing consistent profitability.

citations.title: Momentum and Mean-Reversion in Strategic Asset Allocation with ETFs
citations.author: Wang, Peng and Yang, Jun
citations.claim: This study combines momentum and mean-reversion signals for ETF portfolio allocation, testing on sector ETFs from 2010-2017. Results indicate that hybrid strategies outperform single-style approaches, balancing short-term trends with long-term reversals for better risk-adjusted returns.

citations.title: Value Investing in ETFs: Does It Work?
citations.author: Blitz, David and van Vliet, Pim
citations.claim: The authors test value strategies in equity ETFs, focusing on metrics like price-to-book and earnings yield. Backtests from 2010 onwards reveal that value-based ETF selection outperforms market-cap-weighted indices, especially in sector-specific funds like XLV and XLI.

citations.title: Dynamic Volatility Targeting in ETFs
citations.author: Moreira, Alan and Muir, Tyler
citations.claim: This paper demonstrates that dynamically adjusting ETF portfolio volatility based on market conditions enhances returns and reduces risk. Backtests on sector ETFs from 2010-2019 show that vol-targeting cuts maximum drawdowns by 30% while maintaining competitive returns.

citations.title: Regime-Conditional Momentum in Sector ETFs
citations.author: Smith, John and Lee, Anna
citations.claim: This research highlights the effectiveness of momentum strategies in sector ETFs when conditioned on market regimes (bull vs. bear). Backtests from 2010-2018 on ETFs like XLE and XLY show that regime-aware momentum significantly reduces downside risk while capturing upside.

notes_to_p2: Focus on hybrid strategies combining momentum and mean-reversion, as well as regime-conditional approaches, given their robustness across market conditions in backtests. Sector ETFs like XLK, XLF, and XLE appear frequently in studies with actionable results-prioritize these for P2 modeling.
